lines.text: How many numbers from one to one thousand are multiples of four, six or nine?
lines.caption: How many numbers from one to one thousand are multiples of four, six or nine?

lines.text: Just adding them all up is a trap!
lines.caption: Just adding them all up is a trap!

lines.text: How many whole numbers from one to one thousand
lines.caption: How many whole numbers from one to one thousand

lines.text: are multiples of at least one of four, six and nine?
lines.caption: are multiples of at least one of four, six and nine?

lines.text: Look at twelve. It's a multiple of four AND six.
lines.caption: Look at twelve. It's a multiple of four AND six.

lines.text: So it gets counted twice! Twenty-four and thirty-six sneak in twice too.
lines.caption: So it gets counted twice! Twenty-four and thirty-six sneak in twice too.

lines.text: Fix it. Take away the overlaps, then add back the numbers in all three.
lines.caption: Fix it. Take away the overlaps, then add back the numbers in all three.

lines.text: Five hundred twenty-seven, minus one hundred sixty-five, plus twenty-seven.
lines.caption: Five hundred twenty-seven, minus one hundred sixty-five, plus twenty-seven.

lines.text: That's three hundred eighty-nine, choice C! Most kids stop at five hundred twenty-seven.
lines.caption: That's three hundred eighty-nine, choice C! Most kids stop at five hundred twenty-seven.
